program.ages: ages 11 to 17 (or 10 after finishing 5th grade or earning the Arrow of Light)
program.welcome: New Scouts are welcome all year
about: Scouts BSA is a Scout-led program for youth ages 11 to 17. Scouts plan their own activities, camp and hike, learn real skills, and earn merit badges in hundreds of subjects.
Scouts work in small teams called patrols and advance from Scout to Eagle. Along the way they learn leadership, citizenship, and the outdoors, guided by trained adult leaders.

pillars.title: Scout-Led
pillars.text: Scouts plan and run the program, and adults coach.

pillars.title: Outdoors
pillars.text: Camping, hiking, and high adventure all year.

pillars.title: Advancement
pillars.text: From Scout to Eagle, with merit badges along the way.

pillars.title: Service
pillars.text: Service projects that make a real difference.

groups.name: Scout
groups.text: Learn the Scout Oath and Scout Law and the basics of troop life.

groups.name: Tenderfoot
groups.text: First camping and outdoor skills, first aid, and fitness.

groups.name: Second Class
groups.text: Navigation, cooking, and more time outdoors.

groups.name: First Class
groups.text: Strong outdoor skills and readiness to help others.

groups.name: Star & Life
groups.text: Merit badges, service, and troop leadership positions.

groups.name: Eagle Scout
groups.text: Earned by leading a service project and completing 21 merit badges.

groups_intro: Scouts work in patrols of about 6 to 8 and advance through the ranks at their own pace.

join_steps.title: Contact Us
join_steps.text: Email us with your Scout's name and age. We'll answer any questions.

join_steps.title: Visit a Meeting
join_steps.text: Come to a troop meeting and meet the patrols.

join_steps.title: Apply Online
join_steps.text: Find our troop on BeAScout and complete the youth application.

uniform: Scouts wear the Scouts BSA uniform for meetings and ceremonies and carry the Scouts BSA Handbook. Ask us about used uniforms.

safety.title: Youth Protection
points: Every adult leader completes Scouting America's Safeguarding Youth training and a background check.
Two registered adults are present at every activity. No one-on-one contact between adults and youth.
We post photos of Scouts only with written permission from a parent or guardian, and never with a Scout's full name.

faq.q: When and where do you meet?
Can we visit before we join?
faq.a: Yes! Come to any troop meeting. Email {email} first so we can watch for you.
A small team of Scouts who camp, cook, and work together, with an elected patrol leader.

faq.q: Do parents need to be involved?
faq.a: Scouts lead the troop, and adults support them. We always need adult volunteers; training is provided.
